transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’m here because work has been getting to me a bit. I don’t want to sound dramatic or anything, but I keep feeling like people there—and even some vendors—are kind of tracking what I’m buying and messing with the launch numbers so I look stupid.

My supervisor has shown me reports and says they don’t really prove that, and I get that… I just can’t really shake the feeling. I thought maybe it’d be better to talk to someone before I make it worse or overreact.
Do you think these people are actually plotting against you?

I mean… “plotting” sounds kind of intense, and I don’t want to make it seem like I’m accusing everybody. But yeah, I can’t really shake this feeling that people at work—and even some vendors—are tracking what I’m buying and messing with the launch numbers so I look stupid.

My supervisor has shown me reports that don’t really prove that’s happening, and I understand that, but the feeling still sticks around. I know that probably sounds bad.
Do you think this is something that's been going on for a long time, or is it a relatively new concern for you?

It’s… not brand new, I guess. I didn’t really want to make a big deal out of it, but it’s been maybe around ten months or so that I’ve had these suspicions.

And, um… the voice thing has been around about that long too. I know that probably sounds concerning, but I’m trying to answer it honestly.
You mentioned a 'voice thing' that's been going on for about ten months, can you tell me more about what you mean by that?

Yeah… I mean, it’s not like constant or anything. It’s just sometimes, like when I’m in the stockroom by myself, or driving back from a vendor meeting, I’ll hear this man’s voice like it’s right behind me.

It’ll say things like, “Move faster, Scott,” or kind of laugh at what I picked… like it’s making fun of me. And then I turn around, or look, and there’s nobody there.

I know that sounds weird. I’m not trying to be difficult or anything, I just… that’s what’s been happening.
Does the voice ever tell you to do something that you feel like you have to do?

Not really like… big commands, I don’t think. It’s more like it’ll say, “Move faster, Scott,” like it’s criticizing me or pushing me, especially if I’m in the stockroom. Or it’ll laugh at what I picked.

I mean, I do feel tense when it happens, like I should hurry up, but I wouldn’t say it’s making me do something dangerous or anything. And when I turn around, there’s nobody there. Does that answer what you mean?
Does the voice ever tell you to do something that would hurt yourself or others?

No… no, it hasn’t said anything like that. It’s more just… criticizing me, I guess. Like telling me to move faster, or laughing at what I’m doing.

I know that still sounds bad, but it’s not telling me to hurt myself or anybody else.
Do these thoughts about people tracking you and the voice you hear seem to be all part of one big thing to you, or are they separate things?

I guess they feel connected, yeah… not like I have it all mapped out or anything. I don’t want to sound paranoid.

But what really made me come in is I can’t shake this feeling that people at work, and even some vendors, are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid. And my supervisor has shown me reports that don’t really prove that, so I know maybe I’m overreading it… but it still feels like it’s happening.

The voice feels kind of tied into that, like criticizing me or making me feel watched, if that makes sense. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Do your thoughts feel jumbled or disorganized to you, or do they make sense and follow a logical order?

Um… I think they make sense to me, mostly. Like, in my head there’s a reason I’m thinking each thing, even if I’m not explaining it perfectly.

I don’t know if it comes out jumbled when I talk. I hope not. I might jump around a little because I’m nervous, but it feels like it follows a line to me. Is that… does that answer it?
Are these thoughts and feelings affecting your ability to do your job or take care of daily tasks?

Yeah… I mean, I was trying to tell myself it wasn’t affecting things that much, but it kind of is.

Work has definitely taken a hit. I’ve missed some buying deadlines, and a couple vendor relationships got… strained, I guess. I also made some purchasing calls too fast, without really thinking them through, and my supervisor gave me a formal warning for it.

And outside work, I’ve been pulling back from people. I stopped going to gallery nights and volleyball weekends with my friends, which I used to actually like. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but… yeah, it’s interfering.
Do you think that hearing a voice criticizing you is a normal experience?

I mean… I know it’s probably not, like, a normal thing most people have. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but sometimes when I’m in the stockroom, or driving back from a vendor meeting, I’ll hear a man’s voice like it’s right behind me.

It’ll say things like, “Move faster, Scott,” or kind of laugh at what I picked. And then I turn around and nobody’s there. So… yeah, I guess I know that’s not normal. I just feel embarrassed saying it.
Do your thoughts about people tracking you and the voice criticizing you fit together in a way that makes sense to you, like a story or a theory?

Yeah… I mean, I guess they kind of do fit together in my head, even if I know it probably sounds bad when I say it out loud.

What really made me come in is I can’t shake this feeling that people at work, and maybe even some vendors, are tracking what I buy and messing with the launch numbers so I’ll look stupid. My supervisor has shown me reports that don’t really prove that’s happening, and I get that… but the feeling doesn’t go away.

And then when I hear the voice criticizing me, it sort of lines up with that, like it’s part of the same thing. I’m not saying I’m totally sure, but it feels connected. Does that make sense?
Do you think there's a single explanation or reason behind everything that's been happening to you, including the voice and the feelings of being tracked?

I guess… yeah, there kind of is one explanation my mind keeps going back to.

I don’t want to sound paranoid or like I’m accusing everyone, but what really made me come in is I can’t shake this feeling that people at work — and maybe even some vendors — are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers so I’ll look stupid. Even when my supervisor shows me the reports and they don’t really prove that, it still feels like that’s what’s happening.

I know that probably doesn’t sound great. I’m trying to be honest, though.
Do you think that the people tracking you and the voice you hear are part of a larger plan or scheme?

I mean… I don’t know if I’d call it a whole “scheme,” because that sounds kind of intense. But yeah, in my head it does feel connected.

What really made me come in is I can’t shake the feeling that people at work, and maybe even some vendors, are tracking what I buy and messing with the launch numbers so I end up looking stupid. Even when my supervisor shows me reports and they don’t prove that’s happening, I still keep feeling like there’s something going on behind it.

I know that probably sounds bad. I’m not trying to be difficult or accuse everybody… it’s just hard to turn off.
Do you think the voice and the people tracking you are working together towards a specific goal?

I don’t know if I can say they’re definitely working together, like… I know that sounds like a lot. But it feels like the same goal, I guess.

Like, what really got me worried is I can’t shake this feeling that people at work, and maybe even some vendors, are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers so I’ll look stupid. Even when my supervisor shows me the reports and they don’t actually prove that, I still keep coming back to it.

I’m not trying to make it sound bigger than it is. That’s just how it feels to me.
Do you think all these things that are happening to you, like the voice and people tracking you, fit together in a way that makes sense, like a story or a theory?

Yeah… I mean, I guess my brain does make it into a kind of story, even if I know that probably sounds bad.

It’s like I keep coming back to this idea that people at work, and maybe even vendors, are watching what I’m buying and then messing with the launch numbers so I’ll look stupid. And my supervisor has shown me reports that don’t really prove that’s happening, so I get that I might not be seeing it clearly… but the feeling is still there.

I don’t want to make it sound like I’m totally sure or anything. It just… fits together that way in my head, if that makes sense.
Do you think it's possible that the people tracking you and messing with the launch numbers might not actually be doing that, or is that something you're completely certain about?

I wouldn’t say I’m completely certain… I know there’s a chance I’m wrong. I don’t want to sound like I’m accusing people without proof.

It’s just that what made me come in is I really can’t shake it — this feeling that people at work, and maybe even some vendors, are tracking what I buy and messing with the launch numbers so I look stupid. Even when my supervisor shows me reports that don’t prove it, my mind still keeps going back there.

So… I guess I can admit it might not be happening, but it doesn’t feel that way, if that makes sense.
Do you think there's anything that could ever change your mind about people tracking you and messing with the launch numbers?

I mean… I’d like to think evidence could change my mind. Like if someone could really show me clearly that the buys weren’t being tracked and the launch numbers weren’t messed with, I’d want to believe that.

But that’s kind of the problem… my supervisor has shown me reports that don’t prove anything is happening, and I still keep feeling like people at work, maybe even vendors, are doing it to make me look stupid. I know that probably sounds stubborn. I’m not trying to be difficult — I just can’t shake it.
How convinced are you that people are actually tracking you and messing with the launch numbers?

I’m… pretty convinced, I guess. Not 100%, because I know that sounds extreme and I don’t want to accuse people unfairly.

But what really made me come in is that I can’t shake it — the feeling that people at work, and even some vendors, are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid. Even when my supervisor shows me reports that don’t prove that, it still feels like that’s what’s happening.

So maybe… like, more convinced than I want to be? Does that make sense?
Do you think your beliefs about being tracked and the launch numbers being messed with will ever change?

I hope it will change. I mean, I don’t want to be stuck thinking this way, and I know it probably sounds like I’m holding onto it too much.

But honestly… right now it doesn’t feel like it’s going to change easily. What made me come in is that I just can’t shake the feeling that people at work, and maybe even some vendors, are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers so I look stupid. Even when my supervisor shows me reports that don’t really prove that, my mind still goes back to it.

So… I want to say yes, it’ll change, but I’m not sure. I’d like it to, if that’s the right way to put it.
Do you think it's possible for you to be completely wrong about people tracking you and messing with the launch numbers?

I mean… yes, I know it’s possible. I don’t want to act like I’m always right or like I’m accusing people with no room for doubt.

It’s just hard, because what really made me come in is that I can’t shake the feeling that people at work — and maybe even some vendors — are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid. Even when my supervisor shows me reports that don’t prove it, I still keep feeling like something’s going on.

So… I can say it’s possible I’m wrong. I just don’t feel completely convinced that I am, if that makes sense.

target_item.manifestation: What really made me come in is that I can't shake the feeling that people at work and even some vendors are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid, even when my supervisor shows me the reports don't prove that.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether evidence could change the patient's fixed belief that people are tracking his buys and manipulating launch numbers, which directly assesses delusional conviction and resistance to contradictory evidence.

patient.answer:
I mean… I’d like to think evidence could change my mind. Like if someone could really show me clearly that the buys weren’t being tracked and the launch numbers weren’t messed with, I’d want to believe that.

But that’s kind of the problem… my supervisor has shown me reports that don’t prove anything is happening, and I still keep feeling like people at work, maybe even vendors, are doing it to make me look stupid. I know that probably sounds stubborn. I’m not trying to be difficult — I just can’t shake it.

doctor.intent: Determine the level of conviction in the patient's belief about being tracked
doctor.question: How convinced are you that people are actually tracking you and messing with the launch numbers?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: What really made me come in is that I can't shake the feeling that people at work and even some vendors are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid, even when my supervisor shows me the reports don't prove that.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the strength of conviction in the belief that people are tracking buys and manipulating launch numbers, which directly concerns delusional beliefs.

patient.answer:
I’m… pretty convinced, I guess. Not 100%, because I know that sounds extreme and I don’t want to accuse people unfairly.

But what really made me come in is that I can’t shake it — the feeling that people at work, and even some vendors, are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid. Even when my supervisor shows me reports that don’t prove that, it still feels like that’s what’s happening.

So maybe… like, more convinced than I want to be? Does that make sense?

doctor.intent: Determine the level of conviction in the patient's beliefs
doctor.question: Do you think your beliefs about being tracked and the launch numbers being messed with will ever change?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: What really made me come in is that I can't shake the feeling that people at work and even some vendors are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid, even when my supervisor shows me the reports don't prove that.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the patient's fixed belief about being tracked and launch numbers being manipulated is likely to change, which directly assesses the rigidity of delusional beliefs.

patient.answer:
I hope it will change. I mean, I don’t want to be stuck thinking this way, and I know it probably sounds like I’m holding onto it too much.

But honestly… right now it doesn’t feel like it’s going to change easily. What made me come in is that I just can’t shake the feeling that people at work, and maybe even some vendors, are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers so I look stupid. Even when my supervisor shows me reports that don’t really prove that, my mind still goes back to it.

So… I want to say yes, it’ll change, but I’m not sure. I’d like it to, if that’s the right way to put it.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of a fixed, unshakeable belief
doctor.question: Do you think it's possible for you to be completely wrong about people tracking you and messing with the launch numbers?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: What really made me come in is that I can't shake the feeling that people at work and even some vendors are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid, even when my supervisor shows me the reports don't prove that.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about insight and possible wrongness regarding the fixed belief that people are tracking buys and manipulating launch numbers, which corresponds to delusions.

patient.answer:
I mean… yes, I know it’s possible. I don’t want to act like I’m always right or like I’m accusing people with no room for doubt.

It’s just hard, because what really made me come in is that I can’t shake the feeling that people at work — and maybe even some vendors — are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid. Even when my supervisor shows me reports that don’t prove it, I still keep feeling like something’s going on.

So… I can say it’s possible I’m wrong. I just don’t feel completely convinced that I am, if that makes sense.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's persistent delusions of being tracked and the launch numbers being messed with, along with the presence of hallucinations (hearing a voice), meet the criteria for a psychotic disorder. The duration of these symptoms (around ten months) and their impact on the patient's functioning also support this diagnosis.
